summary: The web app's agent sidebar is now an accessible folder tree. Each nested level is indented. On narrow screens the sidebar opens as a modal navigation drawer. The width divider responds the same way to keyboard and pointer, and Escape cancels a drag. The sidebar has stroke-icon controls and a Connected dot. Rows show reported context use and, when a deployment supplies it, Layout C spend. The terminal drawer's code and fonts load during idle time, and its data loads ahead when you point at or focus the terminal button.

replay.detail: No graph replay. Only browser presentation and client-side loading change.

schema.detail: No storage or wire schema change. The client reads context occupancy from the usage summaries it already receives.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No gateway or protocol change. The web build's extension composition module (the entry substituted for src/extensions/build.ts) must now export a useSidebarSpend hook, because the workspace imports and calls it unconditionally. Existing extension compositions without that export fail to bundle. The public build ships an explicit implementation that reports spend as unsupported. Agents without a folder appear in a single Unfiled group. Sidebar search keeps its machine:/host: tokens and name, ref and host matching, and now also reveals matches inside collapsed folders.

downtime.detail: No downtime; a page reload picks up the new sidebar.

manual.detail: Deployments that build the web app with their own extension composition must add a useSidebarSpend export to it before upgrading: either a hook returning their windowed spend feed or one that reports spend as unsupported, as the public composition does. Verify by building the web app with that composition. Public builds need no step.

recovery.detail: Revert the web build to restore the earlier flat sidebar; no stored state needs repair.
